The man filling Russia is Nicholas II. The moustache over Germany is Wilhelm II. Both were first cousins of the King of Britain, and in 1914 they went to war with each other.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The German link is British. George V's father, Edward VII, and Wilhelm's mother, Victoria, were brother and sister — both children of Queen Victoria. That makes George and Wilhelm first cousins.

2/ The Russian link is Danish. George's mother and Nicholas's mother were sisters, daughters of Christian IX of Denmark. Which is why photographs of George and Nicholas together look like a trick of the light.
3/ Between them, Victoria and Christian IX had grandchildren on the thrones of Britain, Germany, Russia, Denmark, Greece and Norway. At the very top, Europe in 1914 was a family with artillery.
4/ The old man at the centre is Franz Joseph, on the throne since 2 December 1848. Sixty-eight years. He had been emperor longer than the German Empire he was allied to had existed.
5/ He died on 21 November 1916, aged 86 — pneumonia, after catching a cold walking in the park at Schönbrunn with the King of Bavaria. His grand-nephew Charles inherited a war that was already lost.

6/ A single portrait per country also hides the churn. Greece spent much of the war with two rival governments, a pro-German king in Athens and a pro-Allied one in Salonica, until Constantine abdicated in June 1917.

7/ Look at it as a group photograph rather than a map. Four of these men ruled empires — Russian, German, Austro-Hungarian, Ottoman — that had all ceased to exist by 1922.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
